chunks: Zurarah ibn A‘yun narrated from Abū Ja‘far عليه السلام, who said:

The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم made al-Madīnah sacred between its two lava tracts, prohibiting its game; and he عليه السلام prohibited in what surrounds it, a barīd by a barīd, that its herbage be cut or its trees be lopped, except the two sticks of the water-drawing camel.

key_terms.النَّاضِحِ: the camel used for drawing water, whose sticks are excepted
key_terms.الْمَدِينَةَ: al-Madīnah, the sacred city referred to in the hadith
key_terms.بَرِيداً: a measured distance defining the surrounding protected zone
key_terms.حَرَّمَ: declared sacred and prohibited certain acts within the designated area
key_terms.صَيْدَهَا: its game animals, whose hunting was prohibited
key_terms.لَابَتَيْهَا: its two lava tracts or rocky grounds marking the sanctuary boundaries

ai.seo_question: What did the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم prohibit within the sanctuary of al-Madīnah and its surrounding area?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم declared al-Madīnah a sacred precinct, forbidding the hunting of its game. It also describes a surrounding protected area in which vegetation and trees were not to be cut, except for a limited practical need.
